```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5, message = FALSE)
library(influ2)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())
has_glmmTMB <- requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly = TRUE)
```

## Search a scientific candidate set

`search_cpue()` searches a **constrained set of model specifications**. It
protects the annual index term, exposure offsets, and essential random or
spatial structure, then compares eligible candidates using a stated native
criterion. The response can be CPUE, a count with an exposure offset, or
another supported response: it need not be a catch.

This adds a different workflow to the existing interfaces:

- `check_cpue()` checks a model; its residual p-values are not term-removal rules.
- `table_criterion()` compares models that have already been fitted.
- `influ_steps()` and `plot_step()` show changes in annual contrasts along a
  prescribed sequence, rather than choosing that sequence.
- `search_cpue()` evaluates legal candidates and records a recommendation,
  together with its constraints, fitting evidence, and stopping reason.

One search uses one model backend, response definition, and family/link. A
common interface across backends does **not** make AIC, conditional AIC, and
LOOIC interchangeable. See [Model comparison](model-comparison.html).

The starting model is a **maximal candidate model**, not necessarily a saturated
model: it contains the terms we are prepared to consider. A saturated model has
enough freedom to reproduce every observation and is not required here.

## A worked glmmTMB lobster example

We use the same simulated lobster observations as the
[main article](influ2.html). Each observation represents one pot, so its
expected response is lobsters per pot. The negative-binomial model accounts
for extra-Poisson variation; month is a random intercept. Soak time is an
ordinary predictor here, not an exposure offset or a likelihood weight.

```{r search-lobster-model, eval=has_glmmTMB}
data(lobsters_per_pot)
lobster_model <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  lobsters ~ year + poly(depth, 3) + poly(soak, 3) + (1 | month),
  data = lobsters_per_pot, family = glmmTMB::nbinom2()
)
```

### Inspect the plan before fitting

Without `refit = TRUE`, the function only prepares a plan. It does not fit
models, calculate criteria, run MCMC, or simulate residuals. We nominate depth
and soak as the only optional terms. The annual term and monthly random
intercept remain in every candidate. A polynomial is one term block: all three
basis coefficients move together.

```{r search-lobster-preflight, eval=has_glmmTMB}
search_plan <- search_cpue(
  lobster_model, year = "year", criterion = "BIC",
  optional = ~ poly(depth, 3) + poly(soak, 3), max_models = 16
)
search_plan
knitr::kable(search_plan$terms[c("term", "protected", "reason")])
```

`criterion = "auto"` uses native AIC for frequentist models and LOOIC for
complete brms models. Here we explicitly choose BIC, which applies a stronger
parameter penalty at this sample size. This is a choice of search criterion,
not evidence that BIC is universally preferable for CPUE standardisation.

### Run a bounded ordering and backward search

The default `direction = c("order", "backward")` first adds converged term
blocks to the protected core, then considers backward deletions. During
ordering, a block can enter even if the criterion worsens: the aim is an
admissible maximal model. Backward moves must improve the criterion. The
recommended fit is the best eligible model **evaluated**, which need not be
the final path entry or a global optimum.

```{r search-lobster-run, eval=has_glmmTMB}
lobster_search <- search_cpue(
  lobster_model, year = "year", criterion = "BIC",
  optional = ~ poly(depth, 3) + poly(soak, 3),
  direction = c("order", "backward"), max_models = 16, refit = TRUE
)
lobster_search
knitr::kable(
  lobster_search$candidates[c("candidate", "formula", "score", "status")],
  digits = 2, row.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(lobster_search$path, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

This example retains both covariate blocks: automated searching need not
delete something. Each distinct candidate is fitted at most once; revisiting
it during backward checking reuses its recorded result. The original fit can
also be reused when its specification and fitting controls match exactly.

```{r search-lobster-plot, eval=has_glmmTMB, fig.cap="Native BIC values for eligible lobster glmmTMB candidates evaluated by the constrained search. The purple point identifies the best evaluated candidate. Year and the monthly random intercept are protected, and the depth and soak-time polynomial blocks are optional. Candidate numbers describe evaluation order, not a continuous model dimension. Lower BIC is preferred within this comparable candidate set; this display is not a residual goodness-of-fit test.", fig.alt="BIC values for four evaluated lobster mixed-model candidates, with the best candidate highlighted in purple."}
plot(lobster_search)
```

### Retrieve the fit and calculate the CPUE index

`selected_model()` returns the retained native fitted model without refitting.
It can go straight into the usual diagnostics and index interfaces. We use
the same fixed reference profile as the [CPUE indices](cpue-indices.html)
article: median observed depth, a 24-hour soak, and monthly random effect zero.
This zero-effect reference is not integration over the distribution of months.

```{r search-lobster-index, eval=has_glmmTMB}
recommended_model <- selected_model(lobster_search)
reference <- data.frame(depth = median(lobsters_per_pot$depth), soak = 24)
recommended_index <- cpue_index(
  recommended_model, year = "year", reference_data = reference,
  units = "lobsters per pot"
)
knitr::kable(index_table(recommended_index), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r search-lobster-index-plot, eval=has_glmmTMB, fig.cap="Standardised expected lobsters per pot from the recommended lobster glmmTMB model, at the fixed depth and soak-time reference profile and monthly random effect zero. The ribbon is a pointwise 95% confidence interval conditional on this fitted model. It does not include uncertainty from searching and choosing the model, and the index is not an area-integrated biomass estimate.", fig.alt="Annual standardised lobster CPUE from the recommended model, with a pointwise uncertainty ribbon."}
plot_index(recommended_index)
```

Search results retain the best native fit by default. `keep_fits = "none"`
retains only the compact report; `keep_fits = "all"` can be useful for a small
shortlist, but spatial or posterior model objects can be large. Printing,
summarising, and plotting the saved search never repeat fits or residual
simulations.

Compact retention limits the stored report and number of retained fits, not
the native fitter's peak RAM. Native LOO calculations for brms and spatial
Hessian calculations can still require substantial temporary memory.

## Explicitly search a non-essential random term

Random effects are protected by default. To ask whether a particular random
term is needed, nominate that **whole term** explicitly. Here we examine the
monthly intercept while holding the annual, depth, and soak specifications
unchanged. This is a second scientific question, not an automatic licence to
discard all random effects.

```{r search-lobster-random, eval=has_glmmTMB}
month_search <- search_cpue(
  lobster_model, year = "year", optional = "1 | month",
  direction = "backward", criterion = "BIC", max_models = 2, refit = TRUE
)
knitr::kable(
  month_search$candidates[c("candidate", "formula", "score", "status")],
  digits = 2, row.names = FALSE
)
```

The coefficients and dispersion parameters are re-estimated in the reduced
fit. Protecting a structure means keeping its **specification**, not fixing
its numerical estimates. A BIC recommendation does not establish that removing
a process is scientifically sensible; inspect uncertainty, residual structure,
and the resulting index separately.

## Annual interactions, exposure, and other backends

For annual-by-season coding such as `fyear:season`, explicitly protect that
annual block. This unexecuted example illustrates a CRA-style specification;
the data and fitted object are supplied by the analyst, not by this vignette.

```{r search-annual-season, eval=FALSE}
plan <- search_cpue(
  seasonal_model, year = "fyear", include = ~ fyear:season,
  optional = ~ poly(depth, 3) + poly(soak, 3), criterion = "BIC"
)
result <- search_cpue(
  seasonal_model, year = "fyear", include = ~ fyear:season,
  optional = ~ poly(depth, 3) + poly(soak, 3), criterion = "BIC",
  refit = TRUE, max_models = 16
)
```

Offsets, fitted rows, likelihood weights, binomial trial counts, and the
response definition must agree across candidates. For counts fitted with
`offset(log(exposure))`, that offset remains present. If the response is
already CPUE, adding an exposure offset again is not an automatic default.
Searches do not silently change the data subset as terms are removed.

The same interface accepts GLM, mgcv GAM, lme4, glmmTMB, complete brms,
sdmTMB, and univariate tinyVAST models, subject to supported formula and
likelihood contracts. Backend-specific restrictions are explicit:

- Smooths are term blocks; essential random or multidimensional smooths remain
  protected unless deliberately nominated. Existing interaction hierarchy is
  preserved without inventing main effects for intentional interaction-only
  annual coding.
- Gaussian mixed models fitted with REML are refitted with ML when searching
  fixed effects, and that conversion is recorded.
- glmmTMB zero-inflation and dispersion formulas remain fixed in this
  increment. The search changes its main conditional formula only.
- A joint sdmTMB delta search needs `component = "occurrence"` or
  `"positive"`. The other formula, shared spatial domain, and process settings
  remain fixed; it is not simultaneous selection of both components.
- Spatial fields, spatiotemporal processes, and meshes are not automatically
  switched on or off. Compare deliberately fitted process alternatives using
  `table_criterion()` and the diagnostic interfaces.
- Explicit positional parameter maps are not automatically remapped when
  terms change. For mapped TMB fits, fit named candidate specifications
  separately, then use `table_criterion()`. Saved sdmTMB process formulas and
  binomial trial counts remain fixed, even if variables in the original call
  have since changed.
- brms searches require new MCMC fits for changed models. Use an explicit
  candidate budget and native sampling controls; incomplete fits or unreliable
  LOO estimates cannot win. This vignette does not run MCMC.

```{r search-other-backends, eval=FALSE}
# Preflight reports only: no refits or new criteria.
search_cpue(gam_model, year = "year", optional = ~ s(depth))
search_cpue(spatial_model, year = "year", optional = ~ depth)
search_cpue(delta_model, year = "year", component = "positive",
  optional = ~ depth)
search_cpue(bayesian_model, year = "year", optional = ~ depth,
  max_models = 6)
```

## What the search can and cannot establish

The report includes every evaluated specification, numerical status, warnings,
criterion, and stopping reason. Failed or incomparable candidates remain
visible but are ineligible. `max_models` counts distinct attempts, including
failures and a reused original fit. Reaching the limit leaves a bounded result,
not a claim that the search finished exploring the candidate set.

The function is a fresh, backend-aware controller inspired by the ordering
and elimination workflow in
[`buildmer`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=buildmer), rather than a call to
`buildmer::buildglmmTMB()` under a different name. Small native ML tests compare
forward and backward BIC selections with buildmer. This does not imply
identical paths, tie handling, random-effect eligibility rules, or finalisation
for every model. The glmmTMB
[model-evaluation vignette](https://glmmtmb.github.io/glmmTMB/articles/model_evaluation.pdf)
also illustrates `stats::drop1()` and `MuMIn::dredge()` workflows. Their ideas
of protected terms, interaction hierarchy, and comparable observations are
useful, but unrestricted all-subsets fitting is not the default here.

Native AIC is the frequentist default; BIC is optional. Native conditional AIC
is available only where supported and validated, not through an invented
generic mixed-model correction. Complete brms candidates use LOOIC rather
than AIC. Comparisons across inappropriate likelihood targets, priors, response
supports, or observations are rejected rather than ranked together.

Finally, the best observation-model score is not proof that the CPUE index
tracks abundance. Searching can favour a spurious specification, and ordinary
intervals after selection understate the full uncertainty if model-selection
uncertainty is ignored. Retain a scientifically justified candidate set, check
the shortlist with `check_cpue()`, and examine index sensitivity using
`plot_compare()` or deliberately chosen step sequences before accepting a
model for assessment.
